So `hS` is exactly "a set of them no two of which interlace" (source 3-4). CLAUSE 1 = field `smoothing_preserves_order` (SF:298-303) vs source 4-6 ("each closed curve produced by smoothing C along S traverses the marked points of Γ_C lying on it in the cyclic order they have on Γ_C"). Expansion: `geoMarkCycle hP` = the coerced `geoMarkList hP` = `Finset.univ.sort` of `Mark P = ZMod n ⊕ Visit P` under the order lifted from `geoMarkKey = traversalKey ∘ geoMarkPosition` (FlatCarriersDefs:127-160), vertex `i ↦ (i,0)`, visit `v ↦ geometricVisitPosition hP v = (edge of v, actual crossing parameter)` (FlatCarriersDefs:77-79; GeometricVisits:12-16; GaussVisits:45-46) — this is Γ with its marked points in traversal order (SM def:gauss, sm-1:249-257). `geoSmoothingSuccessor hP S = (selectedMarkPerm S).trans (geoMarkSuccessor hP)` (FlatCarriersDefs:235-237): at a selected visit `ρ_S v = ρ (visitTwin v)`, elsewhere `ρ_S = ρ` (244-254), i.e. "joins the incoming branch at c₁ to the outgoing branch at c₂ and the incoming at c₂ to the outgoing at c₁" (source proof 15-17; accepted row 135 `SmoothingDefinitionData.reconnect_selected`, Carriers.lean:277-283). `GeoComponent hP S` = cycles of `ρ_S` (258-259) = "each closed curve produced by smoothing"; `geoOwner` = the class of a mark (262-264) = "lying on it". `geoComponentCycle hP S q` is BY DEFINITION `(geoMarkCycle hP).filter (owner = q)` (GeoCarrierCount:355-357), so the first conjunct of the field is `rfl` (decorative: it names "the marked points of Γ lying on L in the cyclic order they have on Γ"). `GeoInheritsMarkOrder hP S` (GeoCarrierCount:564-568) = ∀ carrier q, ∀ mark a of q, `(geoComponentCycle q).next a = ρ_S a`: walking the carrier (iterating ρ_S) visits its marks in the order they have on Γ. CLAUSE 3 = field `refinement` (SF:320-326): not a printed sentence; reading (i) adds it as the printed first sentence instantiated at C = a carrier q of S (AUTHOR_NOTES:3244-3247, 3752-3760). Check of the instantiation. HYPOTHESIS: printed at C = q needs a set S_q of double points of q (crossings with both visits on q, `geoCarrierCrossings`, FlatCarriersDefs:451-454) no two interlacing on Γ_q. Lean needs `S' ∈ Ind hP`, `S ⊆ S'`. Given a printed instance, S' := S ∪ S_q is in Ind(G_P): S is; two members of S_q with all four visits on q interlace on Γ_q iff on Γ, because Γ_q's order is Γ's restricted (clause 1); a member of S_q interlaces no s ∈ S, since a crossing interlacing some s ∈ S has its visits on different carriers (source lem:piececurve Step 1, d1:612-620; library `visits_separated_iff`, CarriersLemma:229). Conversely a Lean instance S' ⊇ S restricted to q is the printed instance with S_q = (S' ∖ S) ∩ retained(q); the extra members of S' on other carriers do not touch q's marks (ρ_{S'} = ρ_{S∪S_q} on q). So the hypotheses match on every instance; the only cost is that a Lean consumer must derive `S' ∈ Ind hP` from "d is a double point of the current carrier" via the separation lemma — a proof obligation, not a statement gap. CONCLUSION: printed = "each closed curve produced by smoothing q along S_q traverses the marked points of Γ_q lying on it in the cyclic order they have on Γ_q". Lean: for every carrier q' of S' there is a carrier q of S with (i) every mark of q' owned by q (SF:322; `geoOwner_refines`, GeoCarrierCount:1785-1791) = "lies in one carrier of S"; (ii) `markList_{S'} q' = (markList_S q).filter (owner_{S'} = q')` (SF:323-325) = the marked points of q' in the order of Γ_q (which by clause 1/2 at S is q's own traversal order) — this conjunct follows from (i) by `List.filter_filter` on two filters of `geoMarkList`, so it is content-light, but it is the correct rendering of "with the induced order"; (iii) `TracedSuccessor hP S' q'` (SF:326) = q' actually traverses that list in that order. ITERATION: the field is quantified over all S' ⊇ S in Ind, and `carrierword` is proved for every independent S, so a chain S ⊆ S₁ ⊆ S₂ ⊆ … (lem:piececurve Step 5, one double point outside H per step; each S_{k+1} ∈ Ind(G_P) by Step 1 at S_k) is handled step by step and also directly from S; the daughter's order is again a filter of `geoMarkList`, so the next step's "Γ_{q_{k+1}}" is well defined. Faithful as the instantiation claimed.

I found no printed consumer or proof step that needs an instance outside {diagrammatic polygons and their iterated carriers}, and the library has no type of general closed curves on which a wider statement could even be written. So the narrowing is a disclosed, content-preserving restriction to the class the source itself defines and uses, not a blocking defect.
